purpose: The Teichner cost law is grossly superlinear in the crossing number of D_{0,1} # J, so the cheapest way to widen the lane would be a smaller diagram for D_{0,1}. This records that there is not one.

searches.method: simplify('global') plus 1-3 rounds of backtrack(steps=20-60), 400 seeds

conclusion: D_{0,1} does not go below 25 and K_1 does not go below 19. D_{0,1} = 6_3 # (-K_1) is 6 + 19 = 25, so the whole of its size comes from K_1, and K_1 does not shrink. This is a negative search result over the stated seeds, not a proof of crossing number.

consequence_for_the_lane.floor: 6_1 is the smallest ribbon knot, so 31 crossings is the hard floor for any Teichner sum on D_{0,1}, and that partner is already done and negative.

measured_cost.35: >12 h, both 35-crossing partners killed at budget

partner_status.8_9, 8_20 (33): EXCLUDED as fibered: adding a fibered ribbon J leaves K_0 and -K_1 unpaired among the fibered prime summands, so Miyazaki still gives non-ribbon and no certificate can exist
partner_status.9_41, 9_46 (34): with Astra, expect about 10 h each

consequence_for_the_lane.after_that: the non-fibered ribbon knots of at most 10 crossings are then exhausted. The next partners are 11-crossing, giving 36-crossing sums, which the cost law puts at roughly 24-48 h each for one partner. The lane does not so much fail as run out of tractable partners.

caveat: None of this bears on whether D_{0,1} is slice. It bounds what this machine can search, nothing more.
